The stacked lockup, 1080x1080, colour emblem and white wordmark on a black disc inside a transparent square. Supersedes both the horizontal monochrome mark and the two earlier rejections of a stacked lockup - see the notes below for why those no longer apply. Disc removed by DARK_PLATE rather than as a flat ground: it is a neutral gradient from #060606 to about #1a1a1a, and a fixed distance-from-black band left its outer half at ~39% alpha, which read as a grey smudge AND became the mark's ink bounds, shrinking the emblem. 5.87:1, blur 0.61, coverage 0.49 - the strongest mark in the pack on every measure. Stem kept as neom-mono-v3 despite being neither mono nor v3, because renaming means touching both pages, the CSS and the pack for no gain.

Two earlier passes rejected a stacked NEOM lockup on proportion: the slot was .relationship-mark--wide, capped at 4.75rem tall and shaped for roughly 2.9:1, so a 1:1 lockup rendered at about a third of its neighbours' size. That cap is why, not the artwork. fit-marquee-marks.py now sizes every mark off its own ink bounds, so a square lockup fills the tile height like any other square mark - neom is out of WIDE_MARKS, out of the --wide CSS rule and out of the --wide class on both pages, and sizes at 1.5x. The proportion objection was real and is now gone; it should not be re-raised against this artwork.

column6: 597x418 on #f7f7f7, fit 1.06x. 7.64:1. RESOLVES the "rejected" note above: the wordmark reads "TOP GRILL" again, because this is real artwork rather than a re-crop of a mark whose pixels had already been sliced away. Reversed via REVERSE_NEUTRAL_INK, and it is the emblem case rather than the wordmark case - the type is red and orange and reads unaided, but the ring and glass outline that carry the emblem's whole shape are black linework, which on this section would leave a red fork floating in nothing.

top-grill exposed a real flaw in the transform. It tested relative saturation, (max-min)/max, which divides by the brightest channel - so on exactly the dark pixels the transform exists for, it divides by almost nothing and any noise reads as strong colour. A black line that JPEG chroma subsampling had fringed to (30,10,15) scored 0.67 saturation and was spared as "coloured" while its cleaner neighbours reversed, which turned top-grill's solid ring into speckle: 28% of the emblem's opaque pixels stayed dark. Absolute chroma does not have that failure - the same pixel measures 20 against a real red's ~200 - and switching to it drops that figure to 3.6%. The four marks already using the transform all held or improved: china-comservice 6.44 -> 7.06, five-seasons-hotel 16.55 -> 17.27, elegancia-arabia unchanged at 13.32, and national-talents-company 3.85 -> 9.74, which had been under-reversing its bilingual type into grey the whole time.
